I own the yellow monopoly but two of its three properties are mortgaged. I also hold the green property Pennsylvania Avenue. I am weighing whether to unmortgage any properties or trade.

I have decided against mortgaging Ventnor or selling my yellows. I will not trade Pennsylvania Avenue to p1. My only viable path is to survive with the yellow monopoly intact.

I cannot unmortgage any properties because I lack the cash to cover the 10% interest. I will end my turn now.

Rolling a 3 or 12 from Indiana Avenue would cost $200 for the B&O or Short Line railroads. That is only a 3 in 36 chance of immediate bankruptcy.

I am calculating how I rolled from Virginia to Indiana. The path passes Penn RR, St James, CC, Tennessee, NY Ave, Free Parking, Kentucky, and Chance. That is nine spaces. I need to verify whether this roll allowed me to land safely on Indiana.

I confirmed that rolling nine spaces from Virginia lands safely on Indiana Avenue, so I passed the orange hotels without paying rent. From this position, only rolls of three or twelve pose a fatal threat at $200 each. A roll of two would cost only $20, leaving me with $15 cash.

I will not re-propose trades. p2 rejected two offers and cannot fund me. p1 wants to bankrupt me so they can take my properties, and they do not want my yellows.

Selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p1 would let them complete the green monopoly once they buy the unowned North Carolina. That would be dangerous for everyone.

Mortgaging Ventnor would still leave me short of the $200 needed to survive a fatal railroad roll. The yellow monopoly is effectively broken because Atlantic and Marvin Gardens are mortgaged, so no base rent can be collected from that set. Ventnor remains the only unmortgaged property that can generate income.

I checked whether p2 would accept a lower offer for Pennsylvania Avenue. They previously rejected $200 and need cash to buy hotels, so they likely will not accept $100 either. Even $165 from a trade would still leave me short of the $200 needed to survive a fatal railroad roll.

A trade plus mortgage would still leave me broke and lose Ventnor rent. I will not re-ask p2 for a lower offer. p1 might pay $165 for mortgaged PA, but that would help them complete the green monopoly and kill me faster. They could also demand yellows or lowball. p1 is the player who will bankrupt me with orange hotels eventually.

Bankrupting to p2 would give them my yellow monopoly and Pennsylvania Avenue at mortgage value. That would be catastrophic.

I am reconsidering selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p1 for $200. This would let me survive the fatal railroad rolls and keep my yellows intact. p1 already owns Boardwalk, Pacific, and Park Place, so they still need North Carolina to complete the green monopoly. I am weighing whether this trade is worth the risk.

I cannot afford North Carolina, so p2 may buy it to block the green monopoly. Selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p1 for $200 would give me enough cash to survive a fatal railroad roll and leave me with $35. I would lose the property but keep my yellows intact.

I am second-guessing the trade with p1. My notes explicitly forbid selling Pennsylvania Avenue to them because they want my yellows and bankruptcy. I have not rolled yet from Indiana, so the fatal railroad risk is only 3 in 36. If I survive, the orange hotels are roughly a full lap away and behind me.

I am calculating the exact number of spaces from Indiana Avenue to St James Place. I need to count forward from Indiana around the board to determine how far I must travel before reaching the orange hotels.

I counted the exact board positions and found that St James Place is 33 spaces away from Indiana Avenue. That distance exceeds a roll of 12, so I will not land there this turn. The orange hotels remain safely behind me.

I corrected my earlier count. Indiana Avenue is position 23, so a roll of 12 lands on Chance at position 35 rather than Short Line. Only rolls of 3 and 12 remain as threats from this spot. I am now tallying the exact dice combinations for each possible roll.

I have tallied the exact dice probabilities for each possible roll from Indiana Avenue. Only a roll of three is fatal, with two ways to land there. A roll of twelve lands on Chance, which could be dangerous. I am now reviewing the standard Chance cards to see if any advance me toward a property that would cost me money.
